title: What if Andromeda crashed into our galaxy? 🌌
subject: galaxy
description:
Would you want to see Andromeda fill the sky? 👇

What happens when the Andromeda galaxy collides with the Milky Way? It's 2.5 million light-years away and closing in at about 110 km/s, but a 2025 study using Hubble and Gaia data gives the crash only a 50-50 chance in the next 10 billion years.

Sources: ESA/Hubble release heic2508 (Sawala et al., Nature Astronomy, June 2025), NASA via EarthSky, Astronomy.com, Universe Today, Phil Plait (Discover)
tags: what if andromeda hit the milky way

scenes.text: A second galaxy would fill your night sky.
That's Andromeda, 2.5 million light-years away and closing in at about 250,000 mph.
Over billions of years, it grows and warps the Milky Way.
You'd probably never feel the hit. Stars are so far apart they almost never collide.
Gas clouds do, sparking a burst of new stars.
In 2025, Till Sawala's team in Helsinki ran 100,000 simulations with Hubble and Gaia data. Only about half ended in a crash.
